# /fc:risk

[← Back to commands](../commands.md)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Claude name | `/fc:risk` |
| Codex name | `$fc-risk` |
| Kind | Project task — loads `ai-factory/tasks/risk.md` from your repo, so it needs an adopted workspace |
| Description | Assess one spec, plan or change for security threats and delivery risk — findings with severity, status, evidence and mitigation — recorded in one committed file under ai-factory/risks/ |
| Arguments | `<spec or plan path \| working tree \| branch \| diff path>` |

## Usage

Assess one target for security threats and delivery risk: a spec or plan path, the working tree, a branch, or a diff file. The `risk` agent records each finding with its severity, status, evidence and mitigation. Run it before `/fc:spec` or `/fc:plan` to turn threats into open questions and mitigations, or before `/fc:review` on a change. The specifier, planner and reviewer act on the latest applicable section. An assessment gates nothing, and the agent never accepts a finding for you.

The report gives the file path, the target kind and what was assessed, whether the file was created or appended to, the open blocker and major findings, and any category not assessed and why (for example a dependency audit that could not run).

See also: [How it works: the risk triage](../how-it-works.md#the-risk-triage), [workflow.md §5](../../ai-factory/docs/workflow.md#5-every-command).

## Examples

```
/fc:risk ai-factory/specs/PMB-003-csv-export.md
/fc:risk ai-factory/plans/PMB-003-csv-export.md
/fc:risk working tree
/fc:risk branch
```

## Writes

Only under `ai-factory/risks/`:

- A spec or plan: `ai-factory/risks/<ID>-<slug>.md` with the spec's ID, so a spec and its plan share one file; assessing the plan after its spec appends to it.
- A change that matches no existing file: a new risk file with the next free ID.
- A later run on a target already covered appends a dated `## Reassessment` section instead of a new file.

No code, spec, plan or evidence.

## Refuses or asks

- With no input, asks what to assess, and stops. It never guesses the target from the branch name or the last commit.
- When the target has more than one plausible reading, or none, asks you which one and writes nothing; headless, it reports the question and stops.
- With no ID prefix in the project yet, asks for the project name and a prefix interactively; headless, writes nothing and reports why.
